title: helm(private): validate values schema and add rolling upgrade/rollback hooks for init jobs
author: Aisha Kaur
release_notes: Validate values.yaml with values.schema.json and add Helm lifecycle hooks to make init jobs safe across rolling upgrades and rollbacks. No user-facing API changes; primarily chart/operator safety improvements.
description:
Motivation: init jobs used by the Redwood Private Helm chart can run multiple times during rolling upgrades or be re-executed on rollback, which has caused duplicate migration behavior in a customer upgrade (SUP-2122). This PR introduces a strict values schema for the chart to prevent invalid configuration, adds templating helpers for safer init-job rendering, and adds Helm hooks (pre-upgrade/post-rollback) and annotations to ensure init jobs run exactly once during upgrades and are skipped on rollbacks.

What I changed: added values.schema.json for charts/redwood-private, introduced templating helpers in _helpers.tpl to centralize annotations/labels, refactored charts/redwood-private/templates/init-job.yaml to support hook annotations and idempotency markers, added NOTES.txt guidance for operators, and added a small e2e script for upgrade/rollback validation under test/helm-upgrade-rollback.sh.

Key behaviors: pre-upgrade hook will create a short-lived job to perform migrations if and only if .Values.initJobs.enabled is true and .Values.initJobs.runOnUpgrade is true. The job is annotated with a custom idempotency key (chart release + migration-version), and the template renders backoffLimit and ttlSecondsAfterFinished to avoid hung resources. post-rollback hook is configured to mark the idempotency key as rolled-back so corrective actions can be triggered by operator tooling; we intentionally avoid re-running migrations on rollback by default. Values schema enforces structure for initJobs, tolerations, nodeSelector, and resource requests/limits to catch misconfig at lint time.

Testing and CI: ran helm lint and the chart test harness. Initial CI run failed on helm lint due to a missing Chart.yaml keyword and on template lint because of a conditional edge-case with .Values.initJobs.runOnUpgrade when the block was omitted; fixed both by making defaults explicit in values.yaml and adding unit tests for the helper template. Integrated e2e in CI is gated (integration-e2e job) but the PR includes a local test script and instructions in NOTES.txt.

Checklist:
- [x] Add values.schema.json and update Chart.yaml keywords
- [x] Add _helpers.tpl helpers for hook annotations and idempotency keys
- [x] Update init-job template for pre-upgrade/post-rollback lifecycle
- [x] Add default values to values.yaml to avoid nil conditionals
- [x] Add lightweight e2e script and documentation in NOTES.txt
- [x] CI green after fixes

Related: follows earlier work in pr-23810 and pr-23075 around values schema and hook compatibility.

notes_on_rollout: Operators should set values.initJobs.runOnUpgrade explicitly to control migration runs.
Default behavior is conservative: migrations run on upgrade only when enabled; rollbacks do not re-run migrations by default.
Chart maintains idempotency key in job annotation; external operator tooling can inspect this to prevent duplicate runs.
If you rely on custom migration semantics, set values.initJobs.runOnRollback=true and ensure your migration script is idempotent.
